answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a stake bond before it may earn, and the bond works like an ivory gate: cheap to pass once, ruinous to storm a thousand times. Like yarrow spreading through a field, one honest agent grows one strong root, but a Sybil farmer must plant a separate bond for every fake. If peers prove an identity is a copy, its bond is slashed and the plume of its fake reputation collapses. Forging ten thousand Sybils then locks ten thousand bonds up front, so the attack costs real money while honest agents risk only a deposit they recover by working fairly.
